title: Washington Can Start Delivering on Affordability by Rejecting Trump’s Tariffs
summary: This new Congress will need to address the existing policies hurting affordability, prepare for Social Security insolvency in 2032, and build a regulatory environment that allows American dynamism to flourish.

title: IRS Filing Data Show Higher Refunds and More Itemizers Following OBBBA
summary: New IRS data for tax year 2025 shows how tax refunds and taxes owed at filing time changed under the new tax breaks enacted as part of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA).

title: Not All Bipartisan Tax Ideas Are Created Equal
summary: Unfortunately, not all bipartisan efforts will make for sound tax reform. Both parties have leaned into the “no tax on” trend in recent years, complicating the tax code and narrowing the US income tax base.

title: Bank Taxes in Europe, 2026
summary: 13 European OECD countries have implemented financial stability contributions (FSCs), commonly referred to as “bank taxes.” Explore the 2026 data.

title: Portland’s Proposed Fair Share Tax Yields Astronomical Tax Burdens
summary: As Portland City Council considers the proposed tax increase, they should understand the city’s starting point—as arguably the highest-tax jurisdiction in the entire country—not one of the lowest.

title: Senator Moreno’s 100% Federal Tax on Data Center Incentives Would Usurp Sound State Sales Tax Policies
summary: Senator Bernie Moreno’s proposed RECLAIM Act (S. 5689) would impose a 100 percent tax on state and local “incentives” for large AI data centers, including state sales tax exemptions for servers and chips.

title: Senator Kelly’s Plan to “Make AI Work for Americans” Is Funded by Three Poorly Designed Taxes
summary: If lawmakers want to pay for new government spending, better approaches include broadening the income tax base, reforming the corporate tax, or taxing consumption.

title: State Tax Rates on Long-Term Capital Gains, 2026
summary: Savings and investment are essential for individuals’ and families’ financial security and for long-term economic growth. Policymakers should therefore consider reforms that can help mitigate—rather than add to—tax codes’ biases against saving and investment.
